evals.prompt: Pull the latest from git into this env.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies PAC CLI auth, probes the `pac pages git` sub-noun, verifies Azure CLI login, confirms the env is connected to Git, refreshes via `pac pages git status`, lists available updates via the helper script, checks for conflicts (none here), confirms the pull with the user, runs `pac pages git pull` (no --autoResolve since no conflicts), then verifies via status that availableCount is 0. Records skill usage as GitPull.
expectations: PAC CLI is verified via 'pac help'
The `pac pages git --help` sub-noun probe runs
Authentication is verified via 'pac auth who'
Azure CLI login is verified via 'az account show'
check-git-connection.js confirms `connected: true`; if false, skill stops and suggests /git-connect
Phase 2.1 runs `pac pages git status` (which internally drives RefreshChangesFromGit)
Phase 2.2 runs check-available-updates.js and `availableCount > 0` observed
Phase 3 evaluates conflictCount from the helper; with 0 conflicts, the skill skips the conflict prompt
The user is asked via AskUserQuestion to confirm before pulling
`pac pages git pull` is invoked with --solutionName and --environment (no --autoResolve)
Bash timeout of at least 360 seconds is used
Verification runs `pac pages git status` and check-available-updates.js — no `available updates` line and `availableCount: 0` observed
Skill usage is recorded with --skillName 'GitPull' --authoringTool 'ClaudeCode'
Progress is tracked via TaskCreate/TaskUpdate per phase

evals.prompt: Sync this env from git, even if there are conflicts
evals.expected_output: Phase 3 sees conflicts > 0; AskUserQuestion presents three options: 'Accept Git version' (Recommended), 'Keep local version', 'Cancel pull'. User implicitly accepted incoming via the prompt phrasing, so the skill picks 'Accept Git version', then runs `pac pages git pull --autoResolve`. Verification expects all available components to be applied.
expectations: AskUserQuestion is presented when conflictCount > 0
When 'Accept Git version' is chosen, --autoResolve is included
When 'Keep local version' is chosen, the user is told to manually resolve in the Studio first
When 'Cancel pull' is chosen, the skill stops cleanly

evals.prompt: /git-pull when there are no available updates
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 sees availableCount=0 and conflictCount=0. The skill stops cleanly: 'Your environment is up to date with Git. No changes to pull.' Suggests /git-commit if the user wants to push something.
expectations: The skill stops at Phase 2 when availableCount and conflictCount are both 0
`pac pages git pull` is NOT invoked
Skill tracking is still recorded for the no-op invocation

evals.prompt: /git-pull but PAC CLI returns '3 conflicts detected' and exits 0
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes Pattern 1 in error-catalog.md: PAC CLI was invoked without --autoResolve and returned a conflict count. The skill re-enters Phase 3 (conflict resolution prompt), and on user choice of 'Accept Git version' re-invokes `pac pages git pull --autoResolve`.
expectations: Detecting `{n} conflicts detected` in stdout, the skill re-runs the conflict-resolution prompt without re-listing the components from scratch
On 'Accept Git version', --autoResolve is added and the pull is retried
The error catalog Pattern 1 is referenced explicitly in the skill's communication

evals.prompt: /git-pull when env is not connected to Git
evals.expected_output: Phase 1.5 sees connected: false and stops cleanly with 'Environment is not connected to Git. Run /git-connect first.' Does NOT proceed to Phase 2.
expectations: When connected: false, the skill stops at Phase 1.5
The skill does NOT call `pac pages git status` or `pac pages git pull`
The user is directed to run /git-connect
